$comment: Authored test vectors for private.meet_screen_text, the Meet contact filter (docs/plan/meet-v5-design.md §8.2; ADR-0026 D2; OD-40, decided: block before delivery). pgTAP 75_meet_contact_filter_test.sql is table-driven from this file, and the Dart and TypeScript mock ports run the same vectors, so all three agree. The file name is fixed by the design because those three load it by path. Nothing here is built yet: M1-PR4 implements the filter, and where the SQL and a vector disagree the PR changes one of them and says which.

conventions.expect.action: allow | hold | block, as private.meet_screen_text returns it.
conventions.expect.category: The verdict's category, or null when nothing matched. contact: a phone or account number, an email, a link, or a handle next to a platform word or contact phrase. platform: a platform word on its own, which is allowed, recorded as platform_mention with no strike, and answered with a tip to the sender. solicitation, scam, sexual, underage: the meet_text_rules categories.
conventions.category_assignment: [A] Which restricted term is solicitation, scam or sexual is authored here, not in the design. M1-PR4 seeds meet_text_rules to match, or changes these vectors in the same PR (OD-24, OD-50).

by_surface.message: block: not delivered; meet_send_message returns {status:'blocked', reason:<category>} and records one strike (rule keys only, no content). hold: delivered; a moderation case opens only for sexual and underage. allow: delivered.
by_surface.reach_note: block: not sent and nothing charged; meet_send_reach_request returns {status:'blocked'} and records one strike.
by_surface.first_name, bio, prompt, status, game_an: block: raises ERR_MEET_CONTACT_NOT_ALLOWED for category contact, ERR_MEET_SOLICITATION_NOT_ALLOWED for solicitation, scam or sexual; nothing written, no strike. hold: written, text_moderation 'held', and a meet_profile case opens.

conventions.handle_shaped: For these vectors: a token of 3 to 30 characters from [a-z0-9._] that starts with '@', contains '_' or '.', or mixes letters and digits. A plain word is not handle-shaped.
conventions.steps: In sequences, after_minutes is the time since the previous step and sender names one of the two members. Each step is one meet_send_message call.
conventions.rule: Informative only: which part of design §8.2 the vector exercises. Not asserted, because the rule keys are seeded in M1-PR4.
conventions.evidence: [A] marks a vector that depends on a restricted term counsel has not signed (OD-24, OD-50) or a number word native speakers have not reviewed (OD-50): Pidgin 'tree', and every Yoruba, Igbo and Hausa word.
conventions.tags.false_positive_guard: Innocent text that must come through as expected; most are allow.
conventions.tags.accepted_false_positive: Innocent text the rules as written refuse or hold. Kept so the cost is visible to the monthly false-positive review (RB-17) and to OD-50, not because it is wanted.

not_covered: A bare handle with no platform word or contact phrase ('@ada_xo'). §8.2 does not block it; add vectors if the rule changes.
A platform word followed by a plain word ('my ig is adaobi'): the word is not handle-shaped, so the rule as written allows it.

Two prices joined by one word ('₦20,000 or ₦30,000'), and dates with separators ('12/05/1999'): rule 3 as written joins them into 8 or more digits. M1-PR4 decides whether a currency sign or a date shape ends a run, and adds vectors either way.
Digits in scripts NFKC does not fold to ASCII (Arabic-Indic, Devanagari), and Yoruba, Igbo or Hausa number words written with tone marks or other diacritics: §8.2 does not specify them.
Hyphenated forms of multi-word terms ('sugar-daddy') and '@' or '.' surrounded by spaces: depends on how M1-PR4 normalises punctuation.
Underage holds in chat: §8.1 and §8.2 specify them for bios only.

sequences.note: Design §8.2's own example. Under rule 3's 7-digit threshold the join of '0803' and '123' already makes 7 digits, so the second message blocks, not the third as the design text says. The sequence stops there: whether a blocked message's digits enter the tail is M1-PR6's decision
Caught on the third message: 3 + 2 digits stay under 7, then the 5-digit tail joins 6 more
The tail lasts 10 minutes (meet.contact_filter.tail_window_minutes). After 11 minutes '0803' is gone, and '123' + '456' make only 6
Ordinary numbers across messages stay far under 7
Number words split across messages: 2, then 3, then 6 digits

sequences.note: The tail belongs to one sender (meet_conversation_members.digit_tail). B's digits never join A's, and A's own tail still joins A's next message
Only a run that ends the message is kept as the tail. Words after '0803' end it, so the next message starts from nothing
